# CX-02 — Native HTTPS virtual hosting, SNI and DNS-alias qualification

**Priority:** P0  
**Scheduling:** After CX-01 source authority; may run with CX-03  
**Backlog coverage:** RF-008–RF-010, RF-037  
**Repository:** `animatedads/alchemy`

**Mission:** Extend our ooRexx HTTPS server for multiple canonical/alias hostnames and certificate selection while retaining RxSock, Foreign Runtime, OpenSSL memory-BIO ownership, firewall protection and v0.4.6 connection-worker semantics.

**Routes:** `rasenfalcon.com` public; `office.rasenfalcon.com/mail` and `/notes` for separate Wire apps; `gateway.rasenfalcon.com` for LDAP-gated Wire operations portal (mail SMTP/IMAP use separate protocol ports); `noc.rasenfalcon.com` is a DNS CNAME to `london1.rasenfalcon.com`, A `213.255.246.44`; `mcp.rasenfalcon.com` is user-managed DNS. Do not assume a shared IPv4 for the other hosts.

**Build:** Host normalization, SNI certificate map, explicitly configured virtual-host aliases, host/path dispatch and defensive mismatch behaviour (including HTTP `421` where appropriate); per-vhost session/cookie isolation; TLS reload/rotation and tests. Do **not** resolve a CNAME on each HTTP request; the HTTP authority remains the hostname the client asked for. Preserve request Host and SNI evidence separately without treating forwarded headers as authority.

**Exit:** Tests prove `noc` request with SNI/Host `noc` routes correctly and has cert valid for `noc`, despite DNS CNAME to `london1`; unknown host, SNI/Host mismatch, host-header attacks, cross-vhost access, expired cert and TLS reload all fail safely. Owned server only.

## Universal Codex execution contract
- Implement in **our** Alchemy/ooRexx components and Wire semantic applications; no Postfix, Dovecot, slapd, Nginx, external webmail, off-the-shelf CMS, or replacement MCP server. Platform OS, OpenSSL and systemd remain acceptable mechanics, not substitute product authorities.
- Inspect `https://github.com/animatedads/alchemy`, component READMEs, tests, revision provenance and newer Library deliveries; use the latest accepted exact revision, not an assumed repository-folder suffix. Record selected versions and SHA-256s. Mark unknown capabilities UNKNOWN and then write missing functionality.
- Respect `GIT_SUBMISSION.md` for real source publication: use `python3 tools/alchemy_submit.py --repo . --package ... --submitted-by CODEX --json` for eligible component deliveries. Do not open or merge ad-hoc source PRs or publish secrets. Separate independent component packages; no vendored copies of sibling Alchemy trees.
- Implement real source **and executable tests**; give complete files/managed delivery with manifest and evidence. Don't return only a plan, fake health endpoint, stub, pseudocode, or test marked PASS by echo.
- Work autonomously on routine choices. Only stop for truly external permissions/secrets/host facts or explicitly gated destructive/live cutover actions. Never claim live qualification from fixtures. No unapproved production service changes, credential issuance or DNS rewrites. Maintain rollback and operator-approval gates.
- Build and test the isolated component(s) and report `PASS`, `FAIL` and `NOT_RUN` with evidence and constraints. Keep network access/authz secrets and raw mailbox contents out of logs.

## v0.4 boundary correction
NOC and Office each get a separate native ooRexx HTTPS **process and instance** with own owner-private-CA **server leaf**, per-device mandatory mTLS **client identity**, strict SNI + Host and no public/default/HTTP fallback. Public apex/www is a **public** server with appropriate own public TLS and no private routes. Use native HTTPS v0.4.7 as source candidate (pin in `public_site/builder.lock.json`) and verify acceptance first.
